messages.subject: A minor update to Deducer
messages.body_plain:
Deducer 0.2-2 has been released and is available for download from any
of the CRAN servers. This minor update has a couple of small bug
fixes, but more importantly resolves the incompatibilities that arose
when the package ggplot2 was updated.

I also noticed that the binary downloads for mac os <10.5 were stuck
at 0.1-0. This was a problem with the CRAN server, and has since been
resolved. If you are running a mac os X prior to snow leapord and have
been unable to install Deducer, try again now, and let me know if
there are any issues.

Happy new year,
Ian

messages.subject: Comparing Deducer VS other GUI's ?
messages.body_plain:
Hello Ian and all.

I just came across deducer through the comment you made in the
revolution blog.
I was wondering how does your software compare to Rcmdr or other R
GUI's that exist by now.

In terms of: speed, ease of use, statistical methods, and so on.

I understand it must be a very basic question, but still, I can't seem
to find a simple answer for it (and I imagine others must be wondering
the same).

All the best,
Tal

After posting this I made some searches (sorry for not making more), and came across this thread:

messages.subject: Re: Comparing Deducer VS other GUI's ?
messages.body_plain:
Wonderful page Ian,
I wish much success for your system, as I believe it will help us all.

I will add some more thoughts:
1) I wasn't able to find where to report bugs (or feature requests), except this forum (which is not a very efficient way for managing this sort of thing). Is there such a place ?
2) Consider adding links to them from the deducer menu itself.
3) A small "bug" - in the data viewer, if my data.frame variable name is too long, I won't be able to read it all. And I can't seem to set/change the length of the dialog box.
4) I wish there was a place for me to follow on the progress of the project. That is: when new releases are made.  And more importantly, when new articles/tutorials are written about it.  This will be especially important once people will be able to (easily!) add their functions to the menus.
My personal preference for such a thing would be a blog (see for example the ones on: www.r-bloggers.com <http://www.r-bloggers.com>).

Great work, thanks a lot!
Tal

On Wed, Jan 20, 2010 at 7:33 AM, Tal Galili <tal.g...@gmail.com> wrote:

No, not as of right now. You can send bugs either here, or to the e-mail listed in the package description.

> 2) Consider adding links to them from the deducer menu itself.
> 3) A small "bug" - in the data viewer, if my data.frame variable name is too long, I won't be able to read it all. And I can't seem to set/change the length of the dialog box.

True. The size of that combo box could be expanded a bit as there is plenty of room around it. If you click on the box you can read the full names (at least on OS X).

> 4) I wish there was a place for me to follow on the progress of the project. That is: when new releases are made.  And more importantly, when new articles/tutorials are written about it.  This will be especially important once people will be able to (easily!) add their functions to the menus.
> My personal preference for such a thing would be a blog (see for example the ones on: www.r-bloggers.com <http://www.r-bloggers.com>).

I will announce new versions of the package here as well as any new plug-ins or academic articles. Video tutorials can be tracked by subscribing to the youtube channel.

If you (or anyone else) is interested in working on a plug-in or contributing to the project, e-mail me off list and I will provide support.

Cheers,
Ian
